simple.meaning: כְּרַז (kᵉraz) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to proclaim.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:29. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּרַז (H3745) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כְּרַז (kᵉraz) / H3745 is traced through Daniel 5:29 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Belshazzar commanded, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.

definitions.full: H3745. keraz [ כְּרַז ] verb denominative Haph`el make proclamation (possibly directly dependent on κηρύξ (D § 37, p. 146 (2nd ed. 183) K l.c. M 67 *), but even then formed as denominative; compare כְּרַו ᵑ7 , Late Hebrew כָּרַז , Syriac Aph`el, Ethpe`el, so Christian-Palestinian Aramaic, Schw Idioticon 46 Schulth Lex.97 ); — Perfect 3masculine plural רִ֫צוּ הַכְּ Dan 5:29 , with עַיל person concerning. כָּרְסֵא see כסא .
